Procedure title: Udbud af rammeaftale om rådgivning og bistand vedrørende udførelse af nye og egenfinansierede videregående forureningsundersøgelser
Description: Region Syddanmark udbyder fem (5) parallelle rammeaftaler om anskaffelse af rådgivning og bistand vedrørende udførelse af nye, egenfinansierede videregående forureningsundersøgelser i Region Syddanmark. Rammeaftalen omfatter rådgivningsydelser i forbindelse med den offentlige forureningsindsats på lokaliteter, der er kortlagt som forurenede, men hvor forureningen ikke er afgrænset, de såkaldte videregående forureningsundersøgelser. Ordregiver prioriterer indsatsen overfor grundvandstruende forureninger i områder med særlige drikkevandsinteresser og indvindingsoplande højest. Forureninger, der medfører en kraftig indeluftpåvirkning, der udgør en akut risiko for sundhed, prioriteres højt. Forureninger, der udgør en risiko for kontakt samt i forhold til overfladevand og natur prioriteres kun i særlige tilfælde. Denne prioritering er politisk og kan ændres i rammeaftalens løbetid. Formålet med de videregående forureningsundersøgelser er overordnet set at: • Karakterisere og afgrænse forurening i jord, grundvand og poreluft og eventuelt indeluft og overfladevand på forurenede grunde. • Skabe overblik og konceptuel forståelse for forureningens omfang, udbredelse og spredningsveje i jord, grundvand, poreluft, indeluft, luft og overfladevand. • Skabe grundlag for en risikovurdering af forureningen i forhold til områdets grundvandsressource, vandindvinding og boliger samt nuværende eller fremtidig følsom arealanvendelse, natur og overfladevand. • Danne grundlag for et afværgeprogram og skitseprojekt, hvis det vurderes nødvendigt på baggrund af risikovurderingen. • Danne grundlag for en revurdering af kildegrundens og eventuelle nabogrundes kortlægningsstatus samt eventuelle nuancering i forhold til Jordforureningsloven. Ordregiver vil tildele rammeaftale til fem leverandører. Metoden for tildeling af konkrete opgaver under rammeaftalerne af de fem rammekontrakter fremgår af rammeaftalen.

normalized.description: The Rosalind Franklin Mission represents the continuation of ESA’s ExoMars programme following the breakup of the inter-Agency agreement with Roscosmos. As such, it replaces the previous Rover & Surface Platform Mission. The main objectives of the Rosalind Franklin Mission are to safely land on the Mars surface, collect and analyse in situ a range of Martian surface and subsurface soil samples, and to demonstrate technologies for planetary exploration. The key elements of the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover are its advanced drilling system, coupled with a sophisticated on-board science laboratory, and its capability to move autonomously on a variety of terrains on Mars’ surface for at least 218 sols (8 months). Sampling down to a depth of 2 metres significantly increases the probability to detect preserved signs of past or even present life. The analysis of soil geo-chemistry will provide a detailed characterisation of the environment and geological history, and possibly provide evidence for the presence of organic compounds. The ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover will be placed on the surface of Mars by an Entry, Descent and Landing Module (EDLM). This module is the main new developmental element of the ExoMars-Rosalind Franklin mission and will require key contributions from European suppliers. The so-called “braking engines” will be provided by NASA as Customer Furnished Items (CFIs). The Rover System comprises the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover Module and the Rover Operations Control Centre (ROCC), the latter developed by and located at ALTEC in Torino (Italy), where the ground operations of the Rover surface mission will be performed. The Rover and its payload will require maintenance and some upgrades to manage obsolescence and ensure compliance with the new mission requirements associated with the 2028 launch scenario. The ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover will benefit from the provision by NASA of Radio-Isotope Heating Units (RHUs). These RHUs are required to support the thermal control system of the Rover, replacing similar units previously provided by Roscosmos. The new flight system also requires the maintenance of the existing Carrier Module and of the Descent Module equipment and subsystems already developed by ESA. The launch services (launcher and launch site facilities) will also be provided by NASA. Airbus Defence and Space Ltd is the Lead Contractor for the Landing Platform Mechanical Thermal and Propulsion System (“MTPS”). As part of their scope of work, Airbus will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) looking for a supplier of the Propulsion Isolation Valves. The Landing Platform will require at least 6 Propulsion Isolation Valves which will be used on the propulsion system.
